Module 4 of 15

LOS III — KFS, sanction and disbursement

The promise, the paper and the money: disclosure, contracting and the last gate before funds move.

Approval is not a loan. Between the credit decision and the money stand India's strictest conduct controls: the standardised Key Facts Statement, a governed contracting packet, conditions precedent, and the direct fund-flow rule. This module teaches each gate and the evidence it must leave behind.

Lesson 4.1 · 20 min

The Key Facts Statement: India's pre-contract disclosure

  • List what a KFS must contain and how APR is computed
  • Explain the KFS as a gate: validity, acceptance, no-undisclosed-charges rule
  • Describe language and comprehension evidence

Lesson 4.2 · 16 min

Sanction, the agreement packet and eSign

  • Distinguish sanction from disbursement and explain sanction validity
  • Describe the execution packet and its integrity evidence
  • Explain conditions precedent vs conditions subsequent

Lesson 4.3 · 16 min

Disbursement and the direct fund-flow rule

  • State the direct fund-flow rule and its limited exceptions
  • Walk the disbursement readiness checklist
  • Explain what happens after initiation: settlement, failure repair, advice
